# Sirach Chapter 37 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_037_page_001.jpg

---

**37:1** Everyone calls themselves your friend, but some friendships are friends in name only.

**37:2** Isn't it a grief that cuts to the very heart when a close companion turns into an enemy?

**37:3** What a wretched thing is the evil impulse! How did it ever come to fill the world with such deception?

**37:4** A two-faced companion is all smiles when things go well for you, but turns against you the moment trouble arrives.

**37:5** A true companion fights alongside you against your enemies and stands by your side when the battle is fiercest.

**37:6** Don't forget a friend in the thick of battle, and don't leave him out when the spoils are divided.

**37:7** Every advisor is quick to give advice, but some advisors are really just looking out for themselves.

**37:8** When you're seeking advice, be careful. Find out first what the advisor has to gain — they may be steering you in a direction that benefits them, not you.

**37:9** An advisor like that will tell you, "This is the right way to go," while standing back to see what happens to you.

**37:10** Don't ask for advice from someone who is suspicious of you, and don't reveal your plans to someone who envies you.

**37:11** And don't ask for advice on the wrong subjects from the wrong people: don't ask a woman about a rival wife, a coward about warfare, a merchant about commerce, a buyer about what to charge, an envious person about generosity, a hard-hearted person about compassion, a lazy person about work, a temporary hire about long-term commitment, or a self-serving employee about important business. None of these people will give you straight advice.

**37:12** Instead, keep company with a person of genuine faith — someone you've seen live by God's commandments, someone whose outlook is like yours, and who will feel genuine sorrow if you make a mistake.

**37:13** But also listen to your own heart — nobody knows you better than you know yourself.

**37:14** Your own instincts can tell you more than seven lookouts posted on a hillside.

**37:15** And above everything else, ask the Most High to guide your steps in the right direction.

**37:16** Every action begins with a word; every deed begins with a decision.

**37:17** The heart is the root of every human initiative; it grows four branches —

**37:18** good and evil, life and death. And the tongue, which controls them all, is the master of every outcome.

**37:19** Some people are brilliant advisors to everyone else — and completely useless when it comes to helping themselves.

**37:20** A polished speaker may still be despised; he may go hungry,

**37:21** because God never gave him genuine wisdom — only the appearance of it.

**37:22** But there are those who are truly wise, even if only for their own benefit — and the fruit of their understanding is real and reliable.

**37:23** A wise person who teaches their community produces reliable results; the fruits of their understanding can be trusted.

**37:24** The wise person will be loaded with blessings, and everyone who sees them will call them fortunate.

**37:25** A person's days are few, but Israel's story has no end.

**37:26** The wise person among their people will inherit an honored name that lasts forever.

**37:27** My child, test yourself over the course of your life. Find out what's bad for you — and don't do it.

**37:28** Not everything agrees with everyone; different people are suited to different things.

**37:29** Don't be greedy about every kind of luxury, and don't throw yourself at every kind of food.

**37:30** Eating too much causes disease, and gorging yourself leads to stomach trouble.

**37:31** Overeating has killed many people. A disciplined person lives longer.
